text:
Sam H.: quick question — hit a flake after rotating the tls secrets for inference-service in prod. pods are Ready=false because healthchecks are failing even though app responds over TLS when port-forwarded. anyone seen this with NLB + NodePort + externalTrafficPolicy=Local?

Priya R.: hmm, did you rotate the secret mount path only, or also updated the k8s Service / targetPort mapping?

Sam H.: only rotated the k8s tls secret (same name). rollout went fine but target group health shows TLS handshake errors. health check is tcp on NodePort (?) not HTTPS.

Mateo G.: if healthchecks are coming from the NLB to nodes you need to ensure targetType is ip and the nodeport is accepting raw TCP. also check externalTrafficPolicy — Cluster vs Local changes source IP and how kube-proxy routes.

Jana L.: can you paste the Service yaml + annotations? sometimes the ALB/NLB annotations change after terraform refactor. :eyes:

Sam H.: here's the svc snippet we have now:

```yaml
apiVersion: v1
kind: Service
metadata:
  name: inference-service
  annotations:
    service.beta.kubernetes.io/aws-load-balancer-type: "nlb"
spec:
  type: NodePort
  externalTrafficPolicy: Local
  ports:
    - port: 443
      targetPort: 8443
      protocol: TCP
```

Sam H.: target group in AWS is showing Unhealthy with TLSError: tls: handshake failure

Priya R.: ah — health check is TCP to nodeport 32000? NLB healthcheck TCP won't do TLS handshake. If your pods expect TLS (8443) and the NLB is doing TLS passthrough, you need the target group protocol to be TLS not TCP, or switch health check to HTTPS on port 8443.

Mateo G.: another gotcha: if we rotated the secret and the old cert used to have SAN for the NLB's host, and new cert doesn't, the handshake may be rejected. But tcp healthcheck wouldn't show that normally. Check the target group protocol and health check config in Terraform.

Sam H.: checking terraform now — module/aws_nlb target_group uses protocol = "TCP" and health_check { protocol = "TCP" port = "traffic-port" }

Jana L.: change health_check.protocol to "TLS" and health_check.port to "8443" (or traffic-port with TLS target group) in TF, and ensure the target group uses TLS if you want TLS-level checks. if you keep TCP checks, they only verify socket open.

Sam H.: would that require changing the k8s svc targetPort? right now service maps 443->8443.

Priya R.: no change required in k8s for targetPort. But if you use TLS health checks the NLB will perform an SSL/TLS handshake to the pod port. That means the pod must present valid cert for handshake (hostname SAN may be validated depending on config).

Mateo G.: also verify kube-proxy mode and that iptables rules are present on the node for that nodeport. externalTrafficPolicy: Local means only nodes with endpoints will accept traffic; make sure the NLB is targeting only those nodes or you will get unhealthy state.

Sam H.: good point — we recently rolled out a daemonset change that filters the readiness port on init containers. maybe affected endpoints list.

Sam H.: quick test I'm about to run: patch svc to externalTrafficPolicy: Cluster to see if healthchecks pass, then revert if that fixes it.

infra-bot: Deployment inference-service/2026-11-02-rot cert-rotate started canary rollout -> 3/5 pods updated

Priya R.: canary is fine, but prefer to fix TG healthcheck. solution path: (1) update terraform TG to TLS + health check port 8443; (2) ensure cert SAN covers expected host (or disable host verification) ; (3) keep externalTrafficPolicy=Local if you need client IP. if you switch to Cluster you'll lose source IP.

Jana L.: if you can't change TG immediately, temporary workaround: set health_check.protocol = "TCP" and point port to the plain nodeport (so socket opens) OR set service to Cluster until rotation completes. both are temporary and have tradeoffs.

Sam H.: ran quick patch to Cluster — NLB target group shows healthy now. rolling back to Local after I update TF. thanks all.

Mateo G.: when you update TF, ping infra for a quick review. small TF snippet we usually use:

```hcl
resource "aws_lb_target_group" "inference" {
  name     = "tg-inference"
  port     = 8443
  protocol = "TLS"
  target_type = "ip"

  health_check {
    enabled  = true
    protocol = "TLS"
    port     = "8443"
    path     = "/healthz"
    matcher  = "200-399"
  }
}
```

Sam H.: copying that into the PR. will open a tiny tf change and link here.

Sam H.: PR: https://git.redwood/infrastructure/merge_requests/412 (adds TLS TG + test plan)

Priya R.: thanks — will review. remember to include rollout notes: which clusters, and that we flip externalTrafficPolicy back to Local after validation. :thumbsup:

Jana L.: and add a note about secret SAN check in the PR description so we don't get surprised again.

Sam H.: will do. last q — any strong opinion on keeping health check path vs plain TLS handshake? our app has /healthz that returns 200 but over TLS only.

Mateo G.: prefer path-level check (HTTPS/TLS) if the app can serve it — more accurate. TLS-only handshake checks are lighter but don't validate app layer. go with path when possible.

Sam H.: thanks team. I'll wait for reviews before applying to prod.
